bundle.name: Italy: cities, coast and food
bundle.description: Eight day-shaped playbooks from the Italian mainland and Sicily — timed-entry museums taken in the order that leaves them empty, two market mornings, a Pompeii day with somebody who can read the walls, a Parmigiano dairy at the hour it is actually made, and one honestly expensive day on a private boat around Capri.
sources: PARTIALLY VERIFIED 2026-09-06: gating facts (opening days, hours, seasonal ferry and cable-car operation, booking and access rules) were checked against the official sources listed below for 8 of 8 days. Prices were NOT systematically verified and remain model estimates — see KI-2026-09-06-d.

playbooks.name: Rome: the Forum at opening, Testaccio at lunch, Trastevere after dark
playbooks.summary: The ancient half done before the heat and the queues, a market lunch in the neighbourhood Romans actually eat in, and the river crossed on foot at the right hour.

sourceTrip.name: Rome and the south, twelve days

stops.title: Roman Forum and Palatine from the Via di San Gregorio gate

location.name: Roman Forum – Via di San Gregorio entrance

stops.notes: One €18 Colosseo–Foro–Palatino ticket covers all three and runs 24 hours from your Colosseum slot, so spend the cool part of it here. Three gates open onto the Forum: Largo della Salara Vecchia is the one every group is dropped at, and Via di San Gregorio, on the Palatine side, is usually walk-up. Tickets are named and released 30 days out on coopculture.it — between April and October the 09:00–10:00 slots go in the first hours.

stops.title: Down the Palatine and out under the Arch of Titus
stops.notes: Come off the Palatine at the Titus end rather than back the way you came: it drops you within sight of the Colosseum's security line with nothing retraced. Fill your bottle at the nasone beside the arch — there is nowhere to drink inside the amphitheatre and the queue for the one bar is longer than the one to get in.

stops.title: Colosseum, levels 1 and 2, on the timed slot
stops.notes: Already paid for on the combo ticket, so nothing to buy here. The slot is an entry window, not a tour: be in the line ten minutes early, then go straight up to level 2, because the ground-level arcade is where everyone else stops and stands. The arena floor and the underground are a separate, dearer ticket that sells out first — if you did not get one, level 2 looks down on the hypogeum anyway.

stops.title: Mordi e Vai, box 15, Mercato Testaccio
stops.notes: Sergio Esposito's stall does one thing: boiled-beef panini soaked in their own gravy. Allesso di scottona is the one to order; picchiapo if they are out. The queue builds 12:30–13:30 and the market winds down around 15:00, so this is not a 14:45 plan. Cash moves the line faster than card. Verified 2026-09-06 (market listings; the market has no working official site): Mercato Testaccio runs Mon–Sat roughly 07:00–15:30 and is shut all day Sunday, with Mordi e Vai serving about 10:00–15:00 — the whole day below is a Monday-to-Saturday day.

stops.title: A supplì at the original Trapizzino
stops.notes: Two blocks from the market on Via Giovanni Branca, and only worth it if you did not have a second panino. Pollo alla cacciatora is the original filling and still the best one; this is the shop the chain grew out of in 2008, not a branch of it.

stops.title: Cimitero Acattolico and the Pyramid of Cestius
stops.notes: €5 suggested donation in the box at the gate, and a colony of cats that live in the pyramid's shadow. Keats and Shelley are signposted and busy; the part worth the hour is the older enclosure against the Aurelian wall, where nothing is signposted at all. Verified 2026-09-06: Mon–Sat 09:00–17:00 with last entry 16:30, so this slot fits — but on Sundays and public holidays (and Easter Monday, 25 April, 1 May, 2 June, 29 June) it closes at 13:00 with last entry 12:30, when a 15:15 arrival finds a locked gate.

stops.title: Over Ponte Sisto into Trastevere
stops.notes: Walk it rather than taking the tram down Viale Trastevere: the bridge is where the light goes copper over the river bend and the buskers have not started yet. Piazza Trilussa on the far side is solid by 20:30, so cross before then and cut straight up Via del Moro.

stops.title: Dinner at Da Enzo al 29
stops.notes: About thirty seats on Via dei Vascellari and a reservations book that only covers the early sitting; without one you leave a name at the door and drink across the lane until somebody shouts it. Cacio e pepe and the fiori di zucca. The carciofo alla giudia is only honest between November and April — the rest of the year it has been somewhere cold for a long time. Verified 2026-09-06: closed Sundays; service is 12:15–15:00 and 19:00–23:00, so 20:30 sits mid-sitting.

playbooks.name: Florence: the Accademia's first slot, the Uffizi after, and the Oltrarno's workshops
playbooks.summary: Both timed museums taken in the order that leaves them empty, then over the river to the streets where things are still made — marbled paper, silk on eighteenth-century looms, wine poured by the people who imported it.

stops.title: Galleria dell'Accademia on the 08:15 slot
stops.notes: €20 plus the €4 booking fee, through b-ticket.com — the state platform, not one of the resellers that adds €20 for the same slot. Entry is a 15-minute arrival window, and the long line on Via Ricasoli is people who do not have one. Closed Mondays. Walk past David to the unfinished Prisoners first and come back to him around 09:00, when the room briefly empties between windows.

stops.title: Coffee and a bombolone standing at Robiglio
stops.notes: Two minutes from the Accademia on Via dei Servi. Drink it at the bar: table service is a legally separate, higher price list and the sign on the wall says so. The bombolone is filled to order, which is the whole difference.

stops.title: Uffizi, timed entry at Door 1
stops.notes: Reserved tickets go in at Door 1. Door 3 is the exchange desk and swallows twenty minutes for nothing — people queue there because it is the first door they reach. The €4 booking fee is per ticket and unavoidable on the official site. From 1 January 2026 an entry from 16:00 onwards costs €16, which is the cheap way in if you would rather do this at the end of a day than the middle of one. Closed Mondays.

stops.title: Lunch at Trattoria Cammillo
stops.notes: Over the Ponte Vecchio on Borgo San Jacopo, family-run since 1945, and full of Florentines rather than of us by 13:30. Book. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday, which catches people out. Ask what the fritto is that day instead of reading the menu. Verified 2026-09-06: closed Tuesday and Wednesday (some listings also show no Thursday lunch), so this day is Friday-to-Monday.

stops.title: Marbled paper at Giulio Giannini e Figlio
stops.notes: Facing Palazzo Pitti; bookbinders on this spot since 1856. Ask to see the marbling tray in the back room — they will show you if the shop is quiet, which it is mid-afternoon and never is at 11:00. A notebook is around €16 and is the only thing sold on this street that was made on it.

stops.title: Antico Setificio Fiorentino, if the appointment comes through
stops.notes: A working silk mill on Via Lorenzo Bartolini, weaving on looms from the 1780s and warping on a machine built to a Leonardo drawing. Visits are by written appointment only and they do say no, so email a week ahead and hold this slot loosely — which is why it sits here as a maybe rather than a plan.

stops.title: Aperitivo at Le Volpi e l'Uva
stops.notes: Six stools in Piazza dei Rossi behind Santa Felicita, pouring small growers by the glass and cutting the crostini to order. Tell them what you drank at lunch and let them pick; that is the entire service model and it is better than any list.

stops.title: The Giardino delle Rose at dusk
stops.notes: Free, and it is the terrace below Piazzale Michelangelo rather than on it: the same skyline, Folon's bronzes standing about in the grass, and none of the coaches. The gate is on Viale Giuseppe Poggi. Verified 2026-09-06: free, open daily from 09:00, closing 20:00 from 1 May to 30 September, 19:00 in April, 18:00 in March and October and 17:00 from November to February — so this 19:15 slot only exists in the May–September window; any other month, move it ahead of the aperitivo.

playbooks.name: Venice: the 08:30 boat to Torcello, Burano from the back, Cannaregio at dusk
playbooks.summary: A day spent entirely north of the Rialto — the empty early vaporetto to the lagoon's oldest church, into Burano over the Mazzorbo bridge, and back for cicchetti on the Ormesini where Venetians still drink.

stops.title: Coffee and a pastry standing at Dal Mas
stops.notes: Opens at 07:00 on the Lista di Spagna, which is otherwise the worst street in Venice. Croissant and a caffè at the bar, then twenty minutes on foot across to Fondamente Nove. Do not plan on eating anything on Torcello before noon — there are two places and they open when they open.

stops.title: Vaporetto 12 from Fondamente Nove to Torcello
stops.notes: The 08:30 leaves half empty and the day-tour boats do not reach Torcello until about 11:00 — that gap is the whole trick of this day. Buy the 24-hour ACTV travel card rather than singles: line 12 alone would eat three of them, and the card covers the way back and the late boats home. Check the departure board for which pontoon at Fondamente Nove; line 12 does not always use the same one.

stops.title: Santa Maria Assunta and the campanile, Torcello
stops.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-06: this stop used to start at 09:30, which was impossible — the basilica complex opens at 10:30 from March to October and 10:00 from November to February, last entry 30 minutes before it shuts (18:00 summer, 17:00 winter). The 08:30 boat still earns its place: it lands you about 09:15 with the island to yourself, so walk out to the Ponte del Diavolo and Attila's throne while the doors are shut. Then climb the campanile first — the stairs are a ramp, the first hour after opening is still empty, and the whole northern lagoon reads as a map from the top. Inside, the Last Judgement mosaic is on the wall behind you as you come in, so you meet it on the way out, which is the right order. One combined ticket covers basilica, campanile and museum; no photography in the church.

stops.title: Over the Mazzorbo bridge into Burano
stops.notes: Get off one stop early at Mazzorbo and walk the long wooden bridge instead of landing at Burano's front door. You pass the Venissa walled vineyard and arrive at the quiet end of the painted houses — the end without the lace shops and the photographers.

stops.title: Lunch at Trattoria al Gatto Nero
stops.notes: Book weeks ahead, and say on the phone if you want the risotto de gò: it is made from the lagoon goby, takes forty minutes, and is cooked for a minimum of two people. On the Fondamenta della Giudecca facing the canal. Closed Mondays. Verified 2026-09-06: closed Mondays, and lunch service does not start until 12:30 — the old 12:00 sitting in this slot did not exist, so the window now opens with the kitchen.

stops.title: Vaporetto 12 back to Fondamente Nove
stops.notes: Already on the travel card. The 14:30 is the last comfortable one — from 15:30 the returning tour groups fill it at Burano and you stand the whole way to Venice with a bag of lace between your feet.

stops.title: The Ghetto Nuovo and the seven-storey houses
stops.notes: Look up in the campo: these are the tallest buildings in Venice because after 1516 the Ghetto could only grow upwards. The five synagogues are reachable only on the museum's guided tour, in English roughly hourly, and they are the reason to come rather than the museum itself. Closed Saturdays and on Jewish holidays. Verified 2026-09-06: closed Saturdays, Jewish holidays, 25 December, 1 January and 1 May; open 10:00–19:00 from 1 June to 30 September and 10:00–17:30 from 1 October to 31 May. Synagogue tours run hourly from 10:30, and the last Friday tour is sometimes dropped for the Sabbath — in the October–May half take the 16:30 tour at the latest.

stops.title: Cicchetti along the Fondamenta degli Ormesini
stops.notes: Start at Al Timon — the moored boat outside is the seating — then work up the fondamenta to Vino Vero. An ombra at each, everything eaten standing. Done properly this is dinner, and it is the last part of Venice still priced for the people who live in it.

playbooks.name: Naples: Pompeii with an archaeologist, the Farnese marbles, pizza in the Sanità
playbooks.summary: The site in the morning with somebody who can read it, everything portable that came out of it in the afternoon at the MANN, and the evening in the neighbourhood the guidebooks used to warn you off.

sourceTrip.name: Campania, a week from a flat in Chiaia

stops.title: Sfogliatella riccia straight from the oven at Attanasio
stops.notes: Behind the station on Vico Ferrovia; you smell it a street before you find it. Riccia, not frolla — the shell should shatter down your front. Ask for one off the tray that has just come out and eat it standing in the paper, which is the only way it works. Verified 2026-09-06: open Tue–Sun 06:30–19:30 and closed Mondays — which, with the MANN shut on Tuesdays, makes this a Wednesday-to-Sunday day.

stops.title: Circumvesuviana from Porta Nolana to Pompei Scavi
stops.notes: Board at Porta Nolana, not Garibaldi: it is the line's origin one stop earlier, and it is the difference between a seat and forty minutes standing in a crush. Take the Sorrento line and get off at Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri, which is the stop for the Porta Marina gate. The Campania Express is the reserved, air-conditioned alternative at roughly five times the fare and is worth it in August.

stops.title: Pompeii from Porta Marina with a licensed archaeologist
stops.notes: Three gates, and which you use changes the day. Porta Marina Inferiore is the station gate and the one online tickets skip the line at; Piazza Esedra sits beside it; Piazza Anfiteatro is at the far end, in the modern town. Entry is €23, named, time-slotted, with a 20,000-a-day cap. A private licensed archaeologist runs about €160 for the group and is what turns a hot field of walls into three hours — ask specifically for the House of the Vettii, reopened in 2023, and for the Villa dei Misteri last, once the coaches have gone. The free first Sunday of the month is exactly as bad as it sounds.

stops.title: Lunch at Il Principe, Piazza Bartolo Longo
stops.notes: Leave the site by the Piazza Anfiteatro gate rather than walking back across it, and this is two minutes away. They cook a handful of dishes reconstructed from Roman sources and it is not a gimmick — the cassata taken from a fresco is genuinely good. Everything within sight of the Porta Marina gate is a coach canteen.

stops.title: Circumvesuviana back from Pompei Santuario
stops.notes: You do not have to walk back to Porta Marina: Pompei Santuario, on the Poggiomarino line, is three minutes from the restaurant and also runs to Napoli Garibaldi. Half-hourly, no air conditioning, and sit on the left for Vesuvius.

stops.title: MANN: the Farnese marbles, the mosaics, the Secret Cabinet
stops.notes: Everything portable from Pompeii is here, which is why it belongs on the same day as the site and not on a different one. Verified 2026-09-06: open Wed–Mon 09:00–19:30 with last entry 18:30, closed Tuesdays — with two 2026 exceptions, open Tuesday 2 June and Tuesday 8 December and shut the Wednesday after each. Go up to the mosaics first — the Alexander Mosaic came back on display in 2025 after its restoration — then the Gabinetto Segreto, a separate small room the desk may give you a timed slot for. The Farnese Bull downstairs is carved from one block of marble and deserves ten minutes rather than a photograph.

stops.title: Pizza at Concettina ai Tre Santi
stops.notes: Fourth generation on Via Arena della Sanità. Book, or take a number and drink a beer in the street with everybody else. Start with the montanara fritta and follow it with a plain marinara — the fried things are what this place does that the famous queue at Da Michele does not.

stops.title: A fiocco di neve at Poppella
stops.notes: Three minutes' walk. One thing only: a small brioche filled with cold sheep's-milk cream, invented in this shop and copied across the city badly. They come straight out of the fridge and there is still a queue for them at nine at night.

playbooks.name: Capri by private gozzo from Amalfi, with lunch at Il Riccio
playbooks.summary: The expensive version of a Capri day, priced at what it actually costs: a wooden boat and a skipper for eight hours, the island circled before the ferries land, a starred lunch above the Blue Grotto and the chairlift up Monte Solaro after it.

stops.title: Santarosa and coffee at Pasticceria Pansa
stops.notes: On the cathedral steps since 1830 and open at 07:30, which almost nothing else in Amalfi is. The santarosa is the coast's own older, sweeter ancestor of the Naples sfogliatella and is only made properly here and in Conca dei Marini, where the nuns invented it.

stops.title: Meet the skipper at the Molo Pennello
stops.notes: Charters load from the left-hand mole, not the ferry quay where the Positano boats fill up. Confirm by 21:00 the night before: the skipper reads the morning sea state and a Force 4 out of the west cancels Capri altogether, not just the grotto. Bring cash for the tip and for the grotto dinghy.

stops.title: Around Capri anti-clockwise: the Faraglioni, the grottoes, a swim
stops.notes: A full-day gozzo with skipper out of Amalfi is €900–1,300 for the boat, not per person, plus fuel — split four ways it costs about what four ferry-plus-tour tickets cost and is a completely different day. Go anti-clockwise so you are through the Faraglioni arch before 10:30, when the tour fleet arrives from Sorrento. The Blue Grotto needs flat calm and a low tide, the transfer in is a separate rowing boat at roughly €18 cash a head, and a skipper who tells you it is shut is telling you the truth. Verified 2026-09-06 on the grotto: entry runs 08:30–18:00 from 1 April to 30 September, 08:30–16:00 for the first half of October and 09:00–14:00 from 16 October to 31 March; it is always shut on 25 December and 1 January, only sporadically open through the winter, and closed outright on any swell — the skippers judge it at the cave mouth each morning from about 09:00.

stops.title: Lunch at Il Riccio
stops.notes: One Michelin star, blue-and-white tiles on a terrace directly above the Blue Grotto, and the only room on the island where the food is the point rather than the view. Book weeks out and ask for a terrace table, then ask to see the dessert room — it is a walk-in fridge they let you choose from. Around €110–130 a head before wine.

stops.title: Villa San Michele

location.name: Villa San Michele di Axel Munthe

stops.notes: Ten minutes from the restaurant. Axel Munthe built it on a Tiberian ruin and the loggia at the far end, with the Egyptian sphinx facing out to sea, is the best view on Capri that does not require a boat or a chairlift. Verified 2026-09-06: open daily from 09:00, closing 19:00 June–August, 18:00 in May and September, 17:00 in April and October, 16:30 in March and 15:30 from November to January — and closed for the whole of February, plus Tuesdays in January. This stop has been moved back to 15:45 so it still fits in the April–October shoulder; from November to January it has to happen before lunch instead.

stops.title: Seggiovia to the top of Monte Solaro
stops.notes: A single-seat chairlift from Piazza Vittoria with your feet swinging over other people's gardens, twelve minutes each way. CORRECTED 2026-09-06: the old note said the last ascent is an hour before closing, which is wrong and cost you the ride. Ascents run 09:15–17:00 in April, May, September and October (last descent 17:30), 09:30–16:00 from November to March (last descent 16:30), and late into the evening only in high summer. The 17:00 start this stop used to carry was the very last chair at best and impossible for five months of the year, so it now goes up at 16:45 — and from November to March both this and Villa San Michele must move ahead of lunch. It also stops in any real wind. If your knees are willing, walk down through the hermitage at Santa Maria Cetrella instead of riding back.

stops.title: Back to Amalfi along the cliffs
stops.notes: The run home passes under Positano at the hour the cliffs turn orange, which is the part of the charter nobody photographs in the brochure. Tip the skipper in cash — €50–80 on a full-day charter is normal and is not included in the quoted price.

stops.title: A lemon granita on the Amalfi seafront
stops.notes: Crushed in front of you from sfusato amalfitano lemons at the kiosk by the roundabout. Two or three euros, and after the day you have just paid for it will taste like the best thing you bought.

playbooks.name: Matera at sunrise, Alberobello's quiet half, Polignano when the cove empties
playbooks.summary: A driving day across two regions that works only if you take each place at the hour nobody else does — the Sassi at first light, the trulli quarter people still live in, and the cove under the Roman bridge after five.

stops.title: Sunrise over the Sassi from the Belvedere di Murgia Timone
stops.notes: Fifteen minutes by car around and across the gorge, on the park side. This is the angle every film of Matera is shot from, and at sunrise the light comes up the Sasso Caveoso first while the Barisano side is still blue. No gate, no ticket, and there will be two other cars.

stops.title: The rock churches: Santa Maria de Idris and San Pietro Barisano
stops.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-06: this stop used to start at 08:15, when every one of these churches is locked. Santa Maria de Idris with San Giovanni in Monterrone and Santa Lucia alle Malve open daily 09:30–19:30, San Pietro Barisano daily 10:00–19:00 — so take Idris on the dot of 09:30 and cross to Barisano after 10:00. One combined ticket covers several (about €3, €5 or €6 for one, two or three) and you buy it at whichever you reach first. Idris is cut into the rock spur with frescoes reached through a tunnel; Barisano is the largest and the coldest, with the drainage niches where the dead were seated upright to dry. Add the Casa Grotta di Vico Solitario for €5 — one room, a mule stall inside the front door, and the only exhibit that explains why the state emptied the Sassi in 1952.

stops.title: Drive Matera to Alberobello
stops.notes: About 70 km and an hour and a quarter, and the SS172 stretch through the Valle d'Itria is the good part. You now leave the Sassi at 11:15 rather than 10:15, because the rock churches do not open until 09:30. Both centres are limited-traffic zones — park outside and walk in. NOT VERIFIED 2026-09-06: Alberobello's exact ZTL hours; what is clear is that access permits go to residents and businesses only, so do not plan on driving to the trulli. Fuel and the odd toll on the card.

stops.title: Rione Aia Piccola, not Rione Monti
stops.notes: Monti is the thousand-trulli postcard and nearly every cone in it is a shop with a man outside offering you a free look upstairs. Cross Largo Martellotta into Aia Piccola, where roughly four hundred trulli are still lived in and nobody will sell you a whistle. Trullo Sovrano, the only two-storey one, takes twenty minutes. Verified 2026-09-06: it opens 10:00–12:45 and 15:30–18:30 (15:30–18:00 November–March), and on this later timing you reach Alberobello at 12:30, so it does not fit — either go straight to its door before 12:45 and walk Aia Piccola after, or pick it up at 15:30 and push the drive to the coast back an hour.

stops.title: Lunch at La Cantina
stops.notes: Twenty seats down a staircase on Vico Lippolis, open since 1958, and there is no walk-in — book it before you leave Matera or eat somewhere worse. Orecchiette with cime di rapa, and the house Primitivo comes in a jug.

stops.title: Drive down to Polignano a Mare
stops.notes: Forty minutes. Park in the paid lots on Via San Vito and walk in: the centro storico is pedestrian and the streets ringing it are a one-way trap that has eaten better drivers than you.

stops.title: Lama Monachile after the crowd has gone
stops.notes: The pebble cove under the Roman bridge is shoulder to shoulder from 11:00 and empty by 17:00, when the cliff throws it into shade and the water goes glass-flat. Swim shoes — it is stones, not sand, and the entry is steep. Walk the terraces above it afterwards toward the Lungomare Domenico Modugno.

stops.title: A caffè speciale at Il Super Mago del Gelo
stops.notes: Mario's bar on Piazza Garibaldi. Ask for the caffè speciale — espresso, cream, lemon zest and amaretto, invented on this counter — and drink it standing up with the rest of the town.

playbooks.name: The food valley from Bologna: curd at 07:00, prosciutto by 09:00, Modena after dark
playbooks.summary: One long day down the Via Emilia with a driver, built around the fact that Parmigiano is made once a day and it is over by eight in the morning — then hams, a baptistery, anolini, a 1605 vinegar loft and Bottura's cheaper room.

stops.title: Car and driver from Piazza Maggiore, 05:50
stops.notes: A driver for the whole day, Bologna–Parma–Modena and back, is €260–300 and is what makes this possible: the dairy is at dawn, the acetaia is somebody's house with no bus to it, and everything after lunch involves wine. The hour on the A1 in the dark is the price of standing at the vats while they are still full.

stops.title: The morning curd at Caseificio San Pier Damiani
stops.notes: Parmigiano Reggiano is made once a day and it is finished by 08:00: copper vats, the curd broken with the spino, twin cheeses lifted out together in a sheet. Book direct with the dairy rather than through a hotel desk — €20–25 including the tasting of 12, 24 and 36 month. Wear something you do not mind smelling of whey, and be early, because they cannot wait for you.

stops.title: Prosciutto cellars at Ruliano, Langhirano
stops.notes: Twenty minutes up into the hills, where the draught off the Apennines does the drying. Ask why the windows are all on one side of the building; the entire method is that one current of air. The 24-month against the 30-month, cut on the blade, is the tasting that matters, and the unsalted Tuscan-style bread it arrives with is not an accident.

stops.title: The Baptistery of Parma
stops.notes: Pink Verona marble outside, and inside a painted dome most people do not look up at for long enough. Antelami carved the portals and the cycle of the months around the interior. One ticket covers the baptistery and the diocesan museum; Correggio's dome in the Duomo next door is free and takes ten minutes. Verified 2026-09-06: baptistery and diocesan museum open daily 10:00–18:00 on one combined ticket valid two days, sold at the museum on the far side of the piazza rather than at the baptistery door.

stops.title: Anolini in brodo at Trattoria Ai Due Platani
stops.notes: Five kilometres out of Parma toward Coloreto and full of Parmigiani at 13:00, which is the test. Anolini in brodo — small, one filling, and the reason to drive out here — then torta fritta with the culatello. Book. Verified 2026-09-06: closed all day Wednesday and on Tuesday evenings, so this day cannot be run on a Wednesday.

stops.title: Acetaia Giusti, Modena
stops.notes: The family has been doing this since 1605, and the barrels in the loft are not 'aged twelve years' — they are a battery topped up for generations, so the number on the bottle is a minimum rather than an age. Take the tasting that includes the Riserva. The supermarket balsamic you have had is caramel and wine vinegar, and you will taste the gap in about a second. Booking required; there is no shop to wander into.

stops.title: Salumeria Giusti, Via Farini 75
stops.notes: Same family, different address: four tables behind a 1605 shopfront, the oldest deli in Italy that has never moved. Cotechino and a plate of gnocco fritto. Buy the vinegar here rather than at the acetaia — same bottles, and you are not carrying them round all afternoon.

stops.title: Dinner at Franceschetta 58
stops.notes: Bottura's other room and the honest answer to Osteria Francescana's booking lottery: the tasting costs a fraction, opens about a week ahead instead of months, and comes out of the same school of kitchen. Sit at the counter. If you did want Francescana itself, its online release is quarterly and gone in minutes — that is a trip planned around a booking, not a booking fitted into a trip. Verified 2026-09-06: open Monday to Saturday and closed Sundays; dinner runs 20:00–24:00 with the last seating at 21:30, so a 20:00 table is the right end of it.

playbooks.name: Sicily's east: the Catania fish market, as high up Etna as the ordinance allows, Taormina at dusk
playbooks.summary: Market at seven, the high slopes of Etna by noon — the summit craters themselves are off limits under the 2026 altitude cap, so the mountain half of this day stops where the ordinance stops it — and a Greek theatre in the last hour of light. Palermo's markets and Monreale are the other Sicily and need their own day — they are four hours west of every stop below.

stops.title: A Piscaria at full volume
stops.notes: Down the steps beside the Fontana dell'Amenano, under the piazza. Swordfish heads on wet marble, prices shouted in Catanese, and Verified 2026-09-06 it runs Monday to Saturday from about 07:00 until 14:00, loudest between 09:00 and 11:00, with the stalls breaking down from 13:30 — and it does not happen at all on Sunday, or on 5 February when the city shuts for Sant'Agata. Buy nothing: this is a place to stand still in and get splashed.

stops.title: Granita di mandorla and a brioche col tuppo at Savia
stops.notes: Opposite the gates of the Villa Bellini, doing this since 1897. Almond, not lemon, and you dip the brioche into it — in a Sicilian summer this is breakfast, not pudding. Pay at the till first and take the receipt to the counter, which is the order everywhere in Sicily and catches everyone out once.

stops.title: Up the SP92 to Rifugio Sapienza
stops.notes: An hour and a quarter through Nicolosi and up past the 2001 flows, which cross the road as fields of black rubble with a bar buried in them. Parking at Sapienza (1,900 m) is free and full by 10:00. It runs about 15°C colder up here than in Catania and there is no shade anywhere above the treeline: boots, a windproof, sunglasses. Verified 2026-09-06: the cable car at Sapienza starts running at 08:30, so a 10:00 arrival is inside its day.

stops.title: Etna Sud: cable car, 4x4 and a guide, as high as the current ordinance allows

location.name: Funivia dell'Etna and the summit craters

stops.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-06, and read this before you book: the summit craters are not currently a plan. Access above roughly 2,800 m has required a guide from the Collegio Regionale delle Guide Alpine e Vulcanologiche since 2013, and after the Christmas Eve 2025 eruption and the activity that followed, an ordinance has capped access at about 2,850 m on both flanks — which for now removes the summit craters themselves, guide or no guide. The cap is reassessed against the INGV Osservatorio Etneo bulletins and can move either way at short notice, so treat the top of this stop as a maybe and confirm the ordinance with the guides the day before. What reliably works is the combined cable-car-plus-4x4-plus-guide ticket, around €98, which takes you up the Valle del Bove side toward the Torre del Filosofo as far as the day's limit. Verified 2026-09-06: the Funivia dell'Etna runs from 08:30, closing 17:45 in high season with the last descent at 17:30 and 16:00 in low season with the last descent at 15:50; during maintenance windows (in 2026, roughly 8–24 April and 5–20 May) the cabins are replaced by 4x4 buses from 1,920 m. It shuts entirely for wind, storms or volcanic activity, and a guide who cancels on you is doing the job properly. Carry cash for the 4x4 leg.

stops.title: Late lunch at Tenuta San Michele
stops.notes: Come off the mountain on the Taormina side instead of dropping back into Catania. Murgo's estate on the eastern slope makes a metodo classico out of nerello mascalese — a sparkling wine from a red grape grown on lava — and feeds you their own pork and vegetables for as long as you let them. Book; it is not a place you turn up at.

stops.title: Park at Lumbi and take the shuttle down
stops.notes: Do not drive into Taormina. The Lumbi multi-storey sits on the approach road, roughly €25 for the day, with a free shuttle that drops you at Porta Messina every fifteen minutes. The alternative is an hour spent reversing down a one-way street with a wall on both sides.

stops.title: Teatro Antico in the last hour of light
stops.notes: Verified 2026-09-06: open daily 09:00–19:45 with last entry at 19:00, so this 17:45 arrival is comfortable and the theatre is yours for the last hour. On set dates in June, July, August and September 2026 the park also runs evening openings to midnight, last entry 23:00. Climb to the top of the cavea and sit on the left: from there Etna lines up exactly in the gap in the scaenae frons, which after a morning standing on it closes the day properly. Midday here is a furnace and a scrum; this hour is neither.

stops.title: Dinner at Osteria RossoDiVino
stops.notes: Down a staircase off Vico De Spuches, a handful of tables, and the only room in orbit of the Corso Umberto that is neither a laminated tourist menu nor a hundred euros. Pasta alla Norma with proper salted ricotta, and Etna Rosso by the glass off the slope you were standing on this morning.
